questions.question: The objective of the "Gadgil Formula," introduced during the Fourth Five Year Plan, was to allocate plan assistance to states based on their:

__
 
• The Gadgil Formula was introduced during the Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969–1974) to allocate plan assistance from the Central Government to states in India.
 
• Its objective was to ensure a balanced regional development by considering various socio-economic factors.
 
• Key Parameters of the Gadgil Formula:
 
• Population (60% weight): States with larger populations were allocated more funds.
 
• Per Capita Income (25% weight): Special attention was given to states with lower per capita income to reduce regional disparities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other parameters
 
 
• Performance (7.5% weight): States were evaluated based on their performance in plan implementation.
 
• Special Problems (7.5% weight): Specific issues unique to states, such as natural calamities, were also considered.
 
• The formula aimed to prioritize equity by directing more resources to states with a lower per capita income.
 
• It ensured that states with larger populations received adequate resources to address their developmental needs.

questions.question:
Identify which of the following statements about agriculture in India are correct.

1. Rabi crops are sown in India from October to December and harvested from April to June.

2. Important crops grown during Rabi in India are paddy, maize, gram, soybean and mustard.

3. Aus, Aman and Boro are three crops of paddy in Assam, West Bengal and Odisha.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 and 3 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The word Rabi is derived from the Arabic language and means “**Spring**”.
 
• Rabi crops are **sown in winter (hence called winter season crops) from October to December and harvested in summer from April to June.**​

*Hence statement 1 is correct.*

 
• statement 2 is incorrect. While gram (chickpeas) and mustard are indeed important Rabi season crops, paddy (rice) and soybean are primarily Kharif crops, sown in the monsoon season (June to July) and harvested in the autumn (September to October).
 
• Maize is grown in both seasons but is more commonly associated with the Kharif season.
 
• The typical Rabi crops include wheat, barley, peas, lentils, and some types of mustard.

*Hence statement 2 is incorrect.*

 
• Though these crops are grown in large parts of India, states from the north and north-western parts such as Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Uttarakhand, and Uttar Pradesh are important for the production of wheat and other rabi crops.
 
• The availability of precipitation during the winter months due to the western temperate cyclones helps in the success of these crops.
 
• In states like Assam, West Bengal and Odisha, three crops of paddy are grown in a year.
 
• These are Aus, Aman and Boro.
 
 
• Aus refers July- August season.
 
• Aman refers to the December- January seasons.
 
• Boro refers march- May seasons, these are the varieties of rice.
 
 

***Hence statement 3 is correct.***

questions.question: Johann Wolfgang Dobereiner discovered that the properties of liquid Bromine lie between the properties of which gas and solid Iodine?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chlorine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Johann Wolfgang Döbereiner**, a German chemist, introduced the concept of **triads** in 1817, where he grouped elements with similar properties into sets of three.
 
• Döbereiner identified that the properties of liquid Bromine lie between those of **Chlorine (gas)** and **solid Iodine** in terms of atomic mass and chemical behavior.
 
• In Döbereiner's triad, the atomic mass of Bromine (approximately 80) is the arithmetic mean of the atomic masses of Chlorine (~35.5) and Iodine (~127).
 
• This observation marked one of the earliest attempts to classify elements based on their chemical properties and atomic masses.
 
• The grouping of Chlorine, Bromine, and Iodine into a triad showed the periodic nature of chemical elements, forming the foundation for the modern periodic table.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Johann Wolfgang Döbereiner:** He was a German chemist who first attempted to classify elements into groups with similar properties, laying the groundwork for the periodic classification of elements.
 
• **Triads:** Döbereiner's triads are groups of three elements with similar chemical properties, where the atomic mass of the middle element is approximately the average of the other two.
 
• **Halogens:** Chlorine, Bromine, and Iodine belong to the Halogen group (Group 17) in the periodic table. They are highly reactive non-metals and form salts when combined with metals.
 
• **Periodic Law:** The work of Döbereiner and other scientists like Mendeleev led to the development of the periodic law, which states that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.
 
• **Modern Periodic Table:** The periodic table organizes elements based on increasing atomic number, with elements in the same group exhibiting similar properties due to having the same number of valence electrons.

questions.question: Which of the following plant tissues is NOT a type of simple tissue?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Xylem'**

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xylem:**

 
 
• Xylem is classified as a **complex permanent tissue** rather than a simple tissue because it consists of more than one type of cell that works together as a unit.
 
• It is responsible for the conduction of water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the rest of the plant.
 
• Xylem is composed of four distinct types of elements: **tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma, and xylem fibres**.
 
• Except for xylem parenchyma, all other xylem elements are dead cells at maturity and have thick lignified walls, which also provide mechanical strength to the plant body.
 
 

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Parenchyma:**

 
 
• Parenchyma is a **simple permanent tissue** made of relatively unspecialized cells with thin cell walls.
 
• The cells are usually living and have large intercellular spaces; they are primarily involved in food storage and photosynthesis (chlorenchyma).
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma:**
 
 
• Collenchyma is a **simple permanent tissue** that provides flexibility and mechanical support to young plant parts like stems and petioles.
 
• The cells are living, elongated, and irregularly thickened at the corners with cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin.
 
• It allows easy bending in various parts of a plant without breaking.
 
 
 
• **Sclerenchyma:**
 
 
• Sclerenchyma is a **simple permanent tissue** that makes the plant hard and stiff (e.g., the husk of a coconut).
 
• The cells of this tissue are dead, long, and narrow with walls greatly thickened due to **lignin** deposition.
 
• These walls are often so thick that there is no internal space inside the cell.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• Plant tissues are broadly divided into two main groups: **Meristematic tissue** (cells capable of division) and **Permanent tissue** (cells that have lost the ability to divide).
 
• Permanent tissues are further categorized into:
 
 
• **Simple Permanent Tissue:** Composed of cells that are structurally and functionally similar (Parenchyma, Collenchyma, Sclerenchyma).
 
• **Complex Permanent Tissue:** Composed of more than one type of cell working together to perform a common function (Xylem and Phloem).
 
 
 
• **Phloem** is the other complex tissue which transports food materials, usually from leaves to other parts of the plant, and consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, and phloem fibres.

questions.question: Through which Constitutional Amendment was Article 21A introduced, mandating free and compulsory education as a Fundamental Right for children between 6 and 14 years of age?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**86th Amendment Act**__.

__
 
• The **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**, inserted **Article 21A** into the Indian Constitution, making education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• This amendment also brought changes to Article 45, which now directs the State to provide early childhood care and education for children below six years of age.
 
• Additionally, it added Clause (k) to Article 51A, which made it a Fundamental Duty of parents or guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children between the ages of 6 and 14 years.
 
• The 86th Amendment Act paved the way for the **Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009**, commonly known as the RTE Act, which operationalized Article 21A.
 
• This historic amendment was a milestone in India's efforts to achieve universal primary education and combat illiteracy among children.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Amendment Act:**
 
 
• Enacted in 1976, it is also known as the "Mini-Constitution" of India due to the extensive changes it brought to the Constitution.
 
• It made India a "socialist", "secular", and "integrity" State by amending the Preamble.
 
• Transferred subjects like Education, Forests, and Protection of Wild Animals and Birds from the State List to the Concurrent List.
 
• Strengthened the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs) and inserted provisions like Article 48A (environment protection) and Article 43A (worker participation in industries).
 
 
 
• **93rd Amendment Act:**
 
 
• Enacted in 2005, it inserted Clause (5) to Article 15, enabling the State to make special provisions for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes, Scheduled Castes (SCs), and Scheduled Tribes (STs).
 
• This amendment allowed for the reservation of seats in educational institutions, including private unaided institutions, except for minority institutions under Article 30(1).
 
• It laid the foundation for the implementation of the 27% reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in central educational institutions.
 
 
 
• **44th Amendment Act:**
 
 
• Enacted in 1978, it reversed some provisions of the controversial 42nd Amendment Act.
 
• It restored the right to property as a legal right under Article 300A, removing it from the list of Fundamental Rights.
 
• It ensured that Articles 20 and 21, dealing with protection in respect of conviction for offenses and the right to life and personal liberty, could not be suspended even during an emergency.

questions.question: The Indian national satellite system (INSAT) program was established in _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1983**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian National Satellite System (INSAT)** was established in **1983** by the Government of India to cater to various needs like telecommunications, broadcasting, meteorology, and disaster warning.
 
• INSAT is a joint venture between the **Department of Space (DOS)** and **India Meteorological Department (IMD)**, alongside other governmental agencies.
 
• The program marked the beginning of India’s **space-based communication era** with INSAT-1B being the first operational satellite launched in **1983** after the failure of INSAT-1A.
 
• INSAT satellites are equipped with **transponders** for telecommunication and broadcasting and provide crucial meteorological data.
 
• It is one of the largest domestic communication satellite systems in the Asia-Pacific region and has greatly enhanced India’s **telecommunication, television broadcasting, and weather forecasting** capabilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **INSAT System Overview:**

 
 
• INSAT satellites serve **telecommunication, television broadcasting, meteorology, and disaster warning** purposes.
 
• The system consists of a series of satellites like INSAT-2, INSAT-3, GSAT series, and more, which have contributed to India’s space capabilities over the decades.
 
• INSAT satellites are positioned in **geostationary orbit**, ensuring continuous coverage over the Indian subcontinent.
 
 
 
• **First Operational Satellite - INSAT-1B:**
 
 
• INSAT-1B was launched on **August 30, 1983**, on a **Delta rocket** from Cape Canaveral, USA.
 
• It provided services like **telecommunication, television relay, and meteorological observations**.
 
• It marked the first successful satellite of the INSAT series, paving the way for further satellite launches.
 
 
 
• **Applications of INSAT Satellites:**
 
 
• They serve as a backbone for **telecommunication networks** and television broadcasting across India.
 
• **Meteorological payloads** help in weather forecasting, cyclone warnings, and disaster management.
 
• INSAT satellites also support **search and rescue operations** by relaying distress signals.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of INSAT Program:**
 
 
• After the success of INSAT-1B, subsequent satellites like **INSAT-2 and INSAT-3 series** were launched with enhanced capabilities.
 
• Modern satellites like **GSAT** series have advanced features, including high-throughput communication services.
 
• The program has significantly contributed to India’s technological and economic growth.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option Analysis:**

• **1972:** India’s **Department of Space** was established in this year, laying the groundwork for INSAT but not the actual launch.
 
• **1983:** This is the correct answer as INSAT became operational with the launch of INSAT-1B, providing communication and meteorological services.
 
• **1997:** INSAT satellites were operational but this year doesn’t mark the establishment of the program.
 
 
 
• **Significance of INSAT:**
 
 
• INSAT has contributed to **economic growth** by enabling efficient telecommunication and broadcasting.
 
• It plays a key role in **disaster warning systems**, saving thousands of lives during natural calamities.

questions.question: The rate of increase in ex-ante consumption due to a unit increment in income is called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**'marginal propensity to consume'.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Marginal propensity** to consume is the rate of increase in ex ante consumption due to a unit increment in income.
 
• Marginal propensity to consume (MPC)** measures how much more individuals will spend for every additional dollar of income.**
 
• MPC is calculated as the **ratio of marginal consumption to marginal income.**
 
• MPC is related to the** so-called Keynesian multiplier**, where** MPC can help predict the economic growth **from a government stimulus.
 
• The multiplier effect **refers to a chain reaction** of consumption by various entities brought about by an i**nitial increase in income.**
 
• An MPC of one means a** person spent all additional income**.
 
• An** MPC of zero** means they **spent none of it** and, instead, invested it.
 
• The formula used to calculate marginal propensity to consume is** change in consumption divided by change in income**, or, MPC = triangle C overtriangle Ytriangle C overtriangle Y
 
• To make this calculation, you first must **determine the change in income **and the** resulting change in spending (consumption).**

questions.question: The curved surface area of a cylindrical pillar is 528 m² and its volume is 1848 m³ . The ratio between its radius and height is ________.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of **Volume (V)** to **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** of a cylinder is given by **r/2**.

r/2 = Volume ÷ CSA = 1848 ÷ 528 = 3.5

⇒ **Radius (r)** = 3.5 × 2 = 7 m

Using CSA = 2πrh ⇒ 2 × (22/7) × 7 × h = 528 ⇒ 44 × h = 528 ⇒ **Height (h)** = 12 m

Ratio of Radius to Height = 7 : 12

**∴ The correct answer is 7 : 12.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** of the pillar = 528 m²

**Volume (V)** of the pillar = 1848 m³

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area of cylinder = 2πrh

Volume of cylinder = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e730a24932b0a26d590cab1c3a1c2c822b0334b4d87f7a3577e412758023e0c1.png] 

Divide Volume by CSA:

⇒ (πr²h) ÷ (2πrh) = 1848 ÷ 528

⇒ r / 2 = 3.5

⇒ **Radius (r)** = 7 m

Now, substitute r in the CSA formula:

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × 7 × h = 528

⇒ 44 × h = 528

⇒ **Height (h)** = 528 ÷ 44 = 12 m

Ratio of Radius (r) to Height (h):

⇒ r : h = 7 : 12

**∴ The correct answer is 7 : 12.**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a Cylinder

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the two circular ends: TSA = 2πr(r + h).

Volume of a Cone

For a cone with the same radius and height as a cylinder, its volume is one-third of the cylinder: V = (1/3)πr²h.

Relationship between r, h, V and CSA

The radius can always be found directly if Volume and CSA are known using the formula r = 2V/CSA.</p

questions.question: To go a distance of 144 km upstream, a rower takes 12 hours while it takes her only 9 hours to row the same distance downstream. What is the speed of the stream?

questions.question: If the sum of lateral surface area and total surface area of the hemisphere is 770 cm², then find the difference of lateral surface area and total surface area of the hemisphere. (in cm²)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

LSA of hemisphere = 2πr² and TSA of hemisphere = 3πr².

Sum = 2πr² + 3πr² = 5πr² = 770 cm².

Difference = 3πr² − 2πr² = πr².

Difference = 770 ÷ 5 = 154 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 154 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of **Lateral Surface Area (LSA)** and **Total Surface Area (TSA)** = 770 cm².

**Formula Used:**

⇒ LSA of Hemisphere = 2πr²

⇒ TSA of Hemisphere = 3πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fcdfa251479b969fc7afe4b9379d2fc0cef874e355a7f6441534bea79c055752.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum = LSA + TSA = 2πr² + 3πr²

⇒ 5πr² = 770

⇒ πr² = 770 ÷ 5

⇒ πr² = 154

⇒ Difference = TSA − LSA

⇒ Difference = 3πr² − 2πr² = πr²

⇒ Difference = 154 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 154 cm².**

Volume of Hemisphere

The volume of a hemisphere is exactly half the volume of a sphere: V = (2/3)πr³.

Sphere Surface Area

For a complete sphere, the surface area is 4πr². Note that a sphere has no distinct base area.

Base Area of Hemisphere

The flat circular face of a hemisphere has an area of πr², which accounts for the difference between TSA and LSA.</p

questions.question: A 240 m long Darjeeling mail running at a uniform speed, crosses a bridge in 40 seconds, and a man standing on the bridge in 12 seconds. What is the length (in meters) of the bridge?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Speed** is constant, so **Distance** is directly proportional to **Time**.

Time to cross **man** (Train length) = 12 seconds → 240 m

Time to cross **bridge** (Train + Bridge) = 40 seconds → (240 / 12) × 40 = 800 m

Length of **Bridge** = Total Distance − Train Length = 800 − 240 = 560 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 560 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Length of **Darjeeling mail** = 240 m, Time to cross **man** = 12 s, Time to cross **bridge** = 40 s.

**Formula Used:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c8d4d7bbe852599da972618d20c036aec4750e35914c8574d574f39824b0d0a6.png] 

⇒ Speed of train = Length of train ÷ Time to cross man

⇒ Speed = 240 ÷ 12 = 20 m/s

⇒ While crossing bridge, Distance = Length of train + Length of bridge (L)

⇒ 20 = (240 + L) ÷ 40

⇒ 800 = 240 + L

⇒ L = 800 − 240 = 560 m

**∴ The correct answer is 560 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is S₁ − S₂. In the **opposite direction**, it is S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s** to **km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Concepts

When a train crosses a **pole/man**, distance = length of train. When it crosses a **platform/bridge**, distance = length of train + length of object.</p

questions.question: A car travels for 40 minutes at a speed of 40 km/h, for another 50 minutes at a speed of 45 km/h and for next 90 minutes at a speed of 60 km/h. What is the average speed (in km/h) of the car for the entire journey?

questions.question: The two adjacent sides of a parallelogram are 12 cm and 5 cm respectively. If one of the diagonals is 13 cm long, then what is the area of the parallelogram?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Observe that the sides **5 cm**, **12 cm**, and **13 cm** form a **Pythagorean triplet** because 5² + 12² = 13².

This means the **diagonal** and the two **adjacent sides** form a **right-angled triangle**.

A parallelogram is a **rectangle** when its sides satisfy the Pythagorean theorem with the diagonal.

**Area of Parallelogram** = Product of adjacent sides = 12 × 5 = 60 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 60 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Adjacent sides **a = 12 cm**, **b = 5 cm**, and diagonal **d = 13 cm**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/487979496d51df842d5a48d1fce7ca5ec4171b48245d4b7fea3086cf11d9369a.png] 

The diagonal of a **parallelogram** divides it into two **triangles** of equal area.

⇒ Area of **ΔABC** with sides 5, 12, and 13 can be found using **Heron's Formula**.

⇒ Semi-perimeter (s) = (5 + 12 + 13) ÷ 2 = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm

⇒ Area of ΔABC = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − d)]

⇒ Area of ΔABC = √[15(15 − 5)(15 − 12)(15 − 13)]

⇒ Area of ΔABC = √[15 × 10 × 3 × 2] = √900 = 30 cm²

⇒ **Area of Parallelogram** = 2 × Area of ΔABC = 2 × 30 = 60 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 60 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Area of Parallelogram

The area is calculated as **Base × Height** or **ab sin(θ)**, where a and b are adjacent sides and θ is the included angle.

Parallelogram Law

For any parallelogram with sides a, b and diagonals d₁, d₂, the relation is **d₁² + d₂² = 2(a² + b²)**.

Properties of Diagonals

The diagonals of a **parallelogram** bisect each other, but they are equal in length only if the parallelogram is a **rectangle** or a **square**.</p

questions.question: After increasing the selling price of an article by 25%, the new price of the article becomes Rs. 250 . Now a discount of 25% is offered on the new price. What would be the profit or loss in percentage on the original price.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When any value is first increased by R% and then decreased by R%, there is always a net loss.

The net loss percentage is given directly by the formula: Loss % = (R² ÷ 100)%

Here, R = 25%. (The absolute value of Rs. 250 is not needed for finding the percentage).

⇒ Net Loss % = (25² ÷ 100)% = 625 ÷ 100 = 6.25%

**∴ The correct answer is Loss of 6.25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price after a 25% increase = Rs. 250

Discount offered on the new price = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Loss = Original Price − Final Selling Price

Loss Percentage = (Loss ÷ Original Price) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/421951bbfbc4e14677dcdf1f54a64e88596ada9a2668ce73cf14a8d10ca2a7f9.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the original price of the article be x.

⇒ x + 25% of x = 250

⇒ 1.25x = 250

⇒ x = 250 ÷ 1.25 = Rs. 200

Now, a 25% discount is offered on the new price (Rs. 250).

⇒ Discount = 25% of 250 = (25 ÷ 100) × 250 = Rs. 62.5

⇒ Final Selling Price = 250 − 62.5 = Rs. 187.5

Since the Final Selling Price is less than the Original Price, there is a loss.

⇒ Loss = Original Price − Final Selling Price

⇒ Loss = 200 − 187.5 = Rs. 12.5

⇒ Loss Percentage = (12.5 ÷ 200) × 100

⇒ Loss Percentage = 6.25%

**∴ The correct answer is Loss of 6.25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is successively changed by x% and y%, the net percentage change is given by: x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100. If it's an increase, use a positive sign; if a decrease, use a negative sign.

Same Increase and Decrease

If a number is increased by R% and then decreased by R%, the net effect is always a decrease (or loss). The effective loss is calculated as (R² ÷ 100)%.

Extraneous Data in Percentage Problems

In questions asking strictly for a final percentage or ratio, the absolute numerical values (like Rs. 250) are not required and can be safely ignored to save calculation time.

questions.question: Find the LCM of 3⁴ × 5² × 7² × 11, 3³ × 5 × 7 × 11² and 3² × 5³ × 11⁴.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **LCM** of numbers expressed as **prime factors**, select every **prime base** present in any of the terms.

Assign the **highest power** (exponent) found for each prime base across all given expressions.

Prime 3: max(4, 3, 2) = 4 | Prime 5: max(2, 1, 3) = 3

Prime 7: max(2, 1, 0) = 2 | Prime 11: max(1, 2, 4) = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 3⁴ × 5³ × 7² × 11⁴.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number 1 = 3⁴ × 5² × 7² × 11¹

Number 2 = 3³ × 5¹ × 7¹ × 11²

Number 3 = 3² × 5³ × 11⁴ (which is 3² × 5³ × 7⁰ × 11⁴)

**Formula Used:**

**LCM** = Product of the highest powers of all **prime factors** involved in the given numbers.

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Highest power of 3:** Comparing 3⁴, 3³, and 3², the highest power is **3⁴**.

⇒ **Highest power of 5:** Comparing 5², 5¹, and 5³, the highest power is **5³**.

⇒ **Highest power of 7:** Comparing 7², 7¹, and 7⁰, the highest power is **7²**.

⇒ **Highest power of 11:** Comparing 11¹, 11², and 11⁴, the highest power is **11⁴**.

⇒ **LCM** = 3⁴ × 5³ × 7² × 11⁴

**∴ The correct answer is 3⁴ × 5³ × 7² × 11⁴.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF of Prime Factors

To find the **Highest Common Factor (HCF)**, take the product of the **lowest powers** of only the common prime factors.

LCM and HCF Property

For any two numbers A and B: **HCF(A, B) × LCM(A, B) = A × B**. This rule applies only to a pair of numbers.

LCM of Fractions

LCM of **Fractions** = (LCM of **Numerators**) ÷ (HCF of **Denominators**).

HCF of Fractions

HCF of **Fractions** = (HCF of **Numerators**) ÷ (LCM of **Denominators**).</p

questions.question: How does modern engineering mitigate risks associated with bridge collapses?

By avoiding construction over water bodies and mountain gorges
